transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Do not touch the machine or try to unplug it while your hands are wet or if there is water on the floor near the plug, as this creates an electric shock hazard. Once you have safely isolated the power, please check behind the small rectangular kickplate at the bottom left of the front panel (the filter cover). Is there a pool of water inside that area? This will help us determine if it's a simple blockage or a more serious internal leak.

I'm standing in socks on the wet floor, is that bad?? The water has run back towards the plug and the floor under it is wet. The fuse box is in the hall and that floor is dry, so I can go there. Should I turn it off now?

Yes, go to the hall and switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box) now. This is essential because water has reached the plug area, creating a serious shock risk. Once you have done that and are safe, do not touch the machine or try to unplug it while there is still standing water on the floor near the socket. After isolating the power safely from the hall, please let me know if you can see any obvious signs of where the water might be coming from (like a loose hose at the back) without touching anything wet.
ok I've turned it off at the fuse box, the machine has stopped. the water is mostly at the front under the door, not the back. I'm not sure if the socket got wet inside though. what now?
Water in a socket is dangerous and requires professional repair. Is there a pool of water inside that area, or is it just damp?
do you mean the little flap at the bottom front? I looked and it's dry behind there. the water is mostly just under the door at the front. what should I do about the socket?

Regarding the socket: because water has run back towards it, you must not use or touch the socket until a qualified electrician has inspected it. Water inside a socket creates a serious shock risk even when switched off at the fuse box if the internal contacts are wet or corroded. Please leave the socket alone and wait for an electrician to check it. For the leak, since the water is pooling under the door but the filter area is dry, the most likely cause is either debris trapped in the rubber door seal (like a coin) holding it open slightly, or a tear in the seal itself. With the power off and the floor safe, please open the door and check the folds of the black rubber seal for any small items caught inside, and see if the rubber looks torn.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok I opened the door and there's a small split in the bottom fold of the rubber seal, and an underwire from a bra stuck right next to it. is that what's causing it?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Yes, that split in the rubber seal is probably what's causing the leak. The underwire likely punctured or held the seal open, allowing water to escape during the wash cycle and run down onto your floor. You must not use the washing machine again until a qualified electrician has inspected the socket and wiring to ensure it is safe. Once the electrical side is sorted, we can look at replacing the door seal. To help with that, could you please tell me the model number of your Beko washing machine? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok the model number on the label is WTK72041W. so should I just leave the socket alone until an electrician comes? my partner is home in 2 hours

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Yes, please leave the socket alone until a qualified electrician comes. Do not use that socket or the washing machine until they have confirmed it is safe to do so. Regarding the leak: yes, the split in the rubber seal caused by the underwire is most likely what let the water out. To fix this properly, you will need to replace the door seal (boot). You can buy a replacement for your Beko WTK72041W online or from an appliance parts retailer—just double-check the listing matches your model number before ordering. If you are comfortable using tools and following instructions carefully, you can replace the seal yourself. It involves removing the front panel of the machine to access the clamp holding the old seal in place. If you would prefer not to do this, or if you need help finding a reliable engineer once your partner is back, let me know.
